notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 58 (Portugal), Village 29 (Portugal), 87 in all, every one a Portuguese stem; by stem about 25 Régionale (among them i-8zdnpj74, i-lmg3b7w1, i-fj4wvjyr, i-a6r4on1s, i-tl347xd9, i-bovow6yg, i-m6r454q2, i-8wowsxlp, i-kzdn8sjf, i-50zppnxr, i-5f9032uh, i-uk9jx2d3, i-b22ax210, i-x46f2da8, i-1pb82k0c, i-vc3bnnf9, i-526ft0rx, i-kd4hafnj, i-ea0oy4md, i-86b8pafs, i-17tnfmjo, i-t43sg1kf, i-ejw6r08q) and 7 Village (c-x16dzww3, c-d8erebz9, c-xcf3s3vn, c-lsf8njbx, c-fq5o8hha, c-2s8ueo4v, c-zm3hotas) bear on the Court's cells, and the rest go well beyond them (cork, Colares, Bucelas, the Azores, the certifying bodies). Beyond the map: Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet and Fortified Wines carry Port and Madeira, Producers & Icons i-ol6ou8ya (Nacional) and c-nbqtlnyu (Gaia), Terroir: Climate & Soil c-88611nvd. Portugal is the most completely covered subject of the group: every Introductory and Certified cell but one has a stem, and the Court's Douro sub-regions, the four extra DOPs, schist with granite, the terraces, Tinta Negra and the single quinta are all asked. Court cells to read with care: the Court prints Alentejo DOP twice in the Certified appellations cell (a repetition, logged by the extractor), and its gloss Single Quinta: Small producers is loose (the Codex rightly teaches one estate's wine, often in an undeclared year). No errors found. One search spent, for amendments since 2023 to the Douro, Vinho Verde, Alentejo and Bairrada rules: none touches a printed cell; a Vinho Verde notice (date to confirm in the Diário da República) makes the sub-region name and the harvest year optional companions on the label, so wines of more than one harvest may carry a sub-region, which leaves c-1wcnttzv's key standing; the Douro measures of 2024 and 2025 are market support, not rule changes. Card, fact and trap numbers count from one.
